holding_summary: Accounting dispute among tenants in common of inherited real estate over taxes, repairs, and rent-collection commissions; the widow-occupant's use of the homestead is discussed only as an incident of cotenancy, not as a letting to a paying occupant.
notes: Tenants-in-common accounting case; no compensated letting of rooms/dwelling to a third party is at issue.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
holding_summary: A boarding-house keeper sued two sets of guests who had contracted for rooms and board for the June-to-October season but left early and refused to pay. The appellate term held the trial court applied the wrong measure of damages, awarding the full unpaid contract price instead of the plaintiff's lost profits. Damages should be limited to the difference between the contract price and what it would have cost plaintiff to board the defendants had they stayed.

quotes.text: the defendants engaged rooms and board at his hoarding-house for the season from June 1 to October 1, 1907
were brought hy plaintiff to recover damages for breach of a contract for hoard and lodgings
The plaintiff is only entitled to the loss of profits which resulted from the failure of defendants to complete their contract.

court: County Court of New York, Albany County
holding_summary: Summary proceeding to remove a vendee in possession under an executory land-purchase contract; court holds a vendee is not a squatter/licensee removable under the summary-proceedings statute.
notes: Vendor-vendee dispute over land contract, not a lodging/room-letting arrangement despite license-vs-squatter language.

holding_summary: Whether a party-wall contribution covenant runs with the land and binds successive grantees; unrelated to occupancy for pay.
notes: Party-wall covenant case; no bearing on lodging/boarding.

holding_summary: Ultra vires and nuisance analysis of a stage-coach company's exterior advertising signs; municipal ordinance on street advertising upheld. No occupancy of dwellings/rooms involved.
notes: Corporate ultra vires / municipal ordinance case about advertising signs, not lodging.

holding_summary: Liquor Tax Law cancellation proceeding turning on whether a building used partly as a church and partly as the pastor's dwelling was used 'exclusively' as a church for purposes of the 200-foot distance rule.
notes: Liquor-license distance case; the dwelling use discussed is the pastor's own residence, not a paying-occupant letting.

holding_summary: Enforcement of a subdivision deed's building-setback restrictive covenant against a defendant building too close to the street line.
notes: Restrictive-covenant/setback case; no compensated occupancy issue.

holding_summary: Receiver's suit to set aside a corporation's chattel mortgage on hotel furniture as an unauthorized corporate act under the Stock Corporation Law; mortgage upheld as a renewed purchase-money mortgage.
notes: Corporate/chattel-mortgage law case; the 'apartment hotel' operated by the mortgagor tenant is mentioned only in passing background facts.

holding_summary: Contract dispute over an exclusive taxicab-stand concession at a hotel entrance, held invalid as contrary to a municipal ordinance restricting hotel cab stands to hotel guests.
notes: Cab-stand concession case; hotel guests mentioned only as the class of persons the cabs may serve, not an issue of room letting.

court: County Court of New York, Otsego County
holding_summary: Peddling-ordinance case invalidating a municipal ordinance that discriminated between vendors using horse-drawn versus hand-drawn carts; unrelated to housing or lodging.
notes: Street-peddling ordinance case; no lodging/boarding content.

holding_summary: Demurrer sustained in a penalty action against a boarding-house keeper for failing to post 'Oleomargarine Used Here' signs, because the complaint failed to allege the oleomargarine was served as a butter substitute.
notes: Food-labeling regulation applied incidentally to a boarding house among hotels/restaurants/saloons generally; the pleading defect decided is unrelated to the legality or character of letting/lodging itself.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
holding_summary: Summary dispossess proceeding against a chattel mortgagee of saloon fixtures/lease; mortgagee not liable for rent absent actual occupation or control of the premises.
notes: Commercial saloon lease/chattel-mortgage assignment case; not about lodging/dwelling occupancy.

court: County Court of New York, Oneida County
holding_summary: Partition action; widow occupying the homestead with her infant son as guardian in socage held not accountable to cotenants for rental value absent an agreement to pay rent or proof of ouster.
notes: Cotenancy/partition accounting case; testimony that other persons 'more or less' occupied the premises with the widow does not establish a paying letting.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
holding_summary: A landlord sued her former tenant for damage done to furniture in a furnished apartment let for eight months. Both sides tried the case, without objection, on the theory that the measure of damages was the cost of repairs, and that theory became the law of the case. The appellate term limited the landlord's recovery accordingly, ordering a new trial unless plaintiff stipulated to reduce the judgment to the proven repair cost.

quotes.text: The defendant rented furnished apartments from the plaintiff and occupied them for a period of eight months.
The defendant rented furnished apartments from the plaintiff and occupied them for a period of eight months.

Where the trial of an action against a tenant of a furnished apartment for damages to the furniture proceeded upon the theory that the test of the measure of damages was the cost of repairs to the furniture, judgment in favor of the landlord must be so limited in amount.

notes: who_was_letting left unclear: opinion does not indicate whether plaintiff let a single furnished apartment as a householder or operated multiple furnished apartments as a business.

holding_summary: Will construction: language directing a legatee to pay over shares of business profits construed as a covenant rather than a void perpetual trust.
notes: Testamentary trust/covenant construction case unrelated to lodging.

holding_summary: Commercial store lease; whether municipal removal of an encroaching stoop and reconfiguration of the store entrance constituted a partial eviction excusing rent. Held no eviction; rent due in full.
notes: Commercial shop-front lease dispute, not a dwelling/lodging arrangement.

holding_summary: Contract to erect an advertising sign on the exterior wall of a building held to create a license, not a lease, because it conveyed no estate or possessory interest in the realty; injunction against interference denied for other reasons.
notes: Applies license-vs-lease doctrine to a wall-advertising contract, not to occupancy of a dwelling/rooms by a person; no compensated occupancy of the premises is at issue, so marked irrelevant despite doctrinal overlap.

holding_summary: School-tuition dispute over whether a family that rented rooms in another district for the school year was 'residing' there for purposes of free public schooling; held yes, resident though not domiciled there.
notes: The family's renting of rooms is background fact only; the holding concerns residence vs. domicile for school-district purposes, not the legal character or regulation of the letting itself. Opinion in dicta cites Stacom v. Moon (a landlady leasing a house to keep a seasonal boarding house, May-October) but that is not this case's holding.
